relations.reading: The corridor invites a bounded attribution study of where a capability is created, maintained and capitalized, rather than inferring its value from the location that books the revenue.

relations.reading: A cross-border follow-up should establish whether the same capability was retained, transferred, duplicated or lost before applying an attribution-gap explanation.

relations.reading: The survivor lens sharpens value discovery: identify the useful capability and its carriers before deciding which legacy form should remain, change or disappear.
